scope: Resolve an open question from the action-skill-subsystem pass: do s2c 0x016B (SetNoticeEventCondition) and 0x016C (SetEmoteEventCondition) have dual dispatch paths beyond Pattern B vftable[9]? Investigation reveals NO parallel dual path - the apparent duplication is a 2-layer single dispatch chain crossing the C++/Lua boundary via LuaActorImpl vtable.

method.step1: Cross-reference the high-switch-enumeration pass (FUN_004DC690 top dispatcher) case 0x16B/0x16C: both fall through to switchD_004dc749_caseD_f - the actor->vftable[9] generic dispatch (Pattern B). Confirmed via existing BCS-Y-0527 attribution.
method.step2: Cross-reference the fun-0058cca0-walk pass (CharaElement::vftable[9] = FUN_0058CCA0) case table: 0x16B and 0x16C are NOT in the explicit case list. They fall to default branch -> FUN_004D8860 (BCS-Y-0280 sub-dispatcher).
method.step3: Cross-reference the pattern-d-subdispatcher pass (FUN_004D8860 sub-dispatcher) case 0x16B/0x16C: both have dedicated 12-byte trampoline entries - case 0x16B -> FUN_00574FE0 (BCS-Y-0548), case 0x16C -> FUN_00574FF0 (BCS-Y-0549). Both trampolines call (*(*(actor_lua_impl) + 0xCC|0xD0))() = LuaActorImpl::vftable[51] | vftable[52].
method.step4: Decomp BCS-Y-0734 (SetNoticeEventConditionReceiver::slot1 = FUN_0089D980) + BCS-Y-0736 (SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver::slot1 = FUN_0089D750). Critical finding: BOTH receiver Receive methods have NO direct callers in the binary - they are exclusively virtual dispatch targets reached via vtable. This confirms the trampolines (BCS-Y-0548/0549) are the C++-to-Lua-Receiver bridges - vftable[51/52] of the LuaActorImpl stored in the actor record resolves to the Receiver::Receive method.
method.step5: Synthesize: the 'dual path' the action-skill-subsystem pass noted is actually a single 2-layer dispatch chain. Layer 1 is C++ network-tier dispatch through the actor vftable[9] chain; Layer 2 is C++/Lua boundary via virtual function dispatch from the actor's stored LuaActorImpl vtable. Not parallel paths.

dispatch_chain_synthesis.wire_arrival: s2c 0x016B or 0x016C packet arrives at FUN_004DC690 (top dispatcher, BCS-Y-0527 family).
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier1_top_dispatch: FUN_004DC690 high-switch case 0x16B/0x16C: NO dedicated case body - falls through to switchD_004dc749_caseD_f label which calls actor->vftable[9](this).
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier2_actor_vftable9: For CharaElement actors (the most common s2c target), actor->vftable[9] resolves to FUN_0058CCA0 (BCS-Y-0561 third router). FUN_0058CCA0's case table does NOT include 0x16B or 0x16C; both fall to default branch.
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier3_default_subdispatcher: FUN_0058CCA0 default -> FUN_004D8860 (BCS-Y-0280 sub-dispatcher) which has its own case table.
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier4_subdispatcher_case: FUN_004D8860 case 0x16B -> FUN_00574FE0 (BCS-Y-0548); case 0x16C -> FUN_00574FF0 (BCS-Y-0549). Both are 12-byte trampolines.
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier5_lua_actor_vtable: Trampoline body: (*(*(*(this+0x88)) + 0xCC|0xD0))() - reads the LuaActorImpl interface pointer stored at actor+0x88, dereferences its vtable pointer at offset 0, indexes vtable[51] (0xCC/4) or vtable[52] (0xD0/4), calls.
dispatch_chain_synthesis.tier6_receiver_dispatch: For actors whose Lua-side implementation is bound to SetNoticeEventConditionReceiver, LuaActorImpl::vftable[51] resolves to BCS-Y-0734 SetNoticeEventConditionReceiver_slot1_Receive_FUN_0089D980. For SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver, vftable[52] resolves to BCS-Y-0736 SetEmoteEventConditionReceiver_slot1_Receive_FUN_0089D750. Both Receive methods then perform RTDynamicCast (ActorBase -> DirectorBase) and route to rich or fallback registration helpers.
dispatch_chain_synthesis.depth_summary: 6-layer dispatch chain from wire to Receiver. Deepest documented dispatch chain in the codebase so far (the 0x00CC-actor-record-apply pass's 0x00CC case was 5-layer; 0x16B/0x16C add the extra Lua-virtual-resolution layer).

key_findings: RESOLVED open question from the action-skill-subsystem pass: 0x016B and 0x016C do NOT have dual dispatch paths. The apparent 'dual path' was a 2-layer view of the same dispatch chain - the C++ trampoline (BCS-Y-0548/0549) + the Lua-Receiver class vtable resolution are stacked layers of one continuous dispatch, not parallel pathways.

BCS-Y-0548/0549 trampolines are the C++-to-Lua-Receiver BRIDGE for vftable[51]/[52] dispatch slots. Their job is to translate the network-tier opcode-keyed dispatch (FUN_004D8860 case 0x16B/0x16C) into the actor-state-tier virtual call (vftable[51/52] on the LuaActorImpl stored in the actor record). Without these trampolines, opcodes 0x16B/0x16C would dead-end at FUN_004D8860's default.

FUN_0089D980 and FUN_0089D750 have NO direct callers in the binary - they are exclusively virtual dispatch targets. This is a structural confirmation that the LuaActorImpl vftable IS the receiver-registration mechanism for this family of opcodes. The receiver-class registry that the receiver-discovery pass cataloged via RTTI doesn't have a separate runtime dispatcher; it relies entirely on C++ MI vtable dispatch.

Implication for client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' Pattern B: the client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' worry about 'Pattern B Receivers don't have a runtime dispatcher' is unfounded for the LuaActorImpl::vftable-resident receivers. They DO have a runtime dispatcher - it's the standard C++ virtual dispatch via vftable[51..53] slots, fed by the FUN_004D8860 sub-dispatcher trampolines. The 23-receiver-class registry is bound to specific vtable slots via class layout. The vtable slot is the indirection mechanism.

Methodology refinement: For any Pattern A trampoline of shape (*(*param_1 + 0xNNN))() where param_1 is the actor's LuaActorImpl interface, the final dispatch resolves to a *Receiver::slot1 Receive method on the actor's specific Lua subclass. This pattern is bridge-cataloged: trampoline BCS-Y attributes to vtable slot, and slot-resident Receiver BCS-Y attributes to specific Receiver class. The two BCS-Y entries together fully describe one dispatch operation.

Other LuaActorImpl vtable[N] trampolines (BCS-Y-0548..0552 covering slots 51/52/53/others) follow the same pattern: each is a C++-to-Lua-Receiver bridge for its specific vtable slot. Future drill targets for opcode attribution: walk each of those trampolines -> vtable slot -> identify the Receiver class subscribed at that slot (via the receiver-discovery pass registry).
